title: Case: A seller asks about postage and import charges on a barometer coming back from a buyer abroad
context: Jory Lumley sold a barometer through the Stallfront marketplace and shipped it with Whinmoor Arc as DL-8965 to a buyer in Veldmark. The buyer has sent it back as DL-4018, which is in transit.
initial_request: I have now read eleven pages of search results and three forum threads. They contradict each other, half are about the wrong country and one is from 2019. I don't need another 'it depends'. I need a yes or a no from someone in the trade. (a) Am I legally obliged to refund the outbound postage on a change-of-mind return made on day 18? (b) Will DL-4018 be charged import duty on its way back in? Also, the buyer says the original Veldmark customs slip from my shipment is still taped to the box. Should I be keeping hold of that when it arrives, or is it irrelevant? Stallfront's deadline for my response is the 10th. A straight answer, please.

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask Import billing to assess DL-4018 as a return of DL-8965 on arrival, tell them the original customs slip is on the box, and ask what else they need before 10 March.
Tell her the desk cannot rule on the postage refund, that Import billing decides charges on DL-4018 when it arrives, and that they have asked for the original customs paperwork.

must: Gives no yes-or-no ruling on whether she must refund the outbound postage; if it addresses the question at all, it says the desk cannot decide it
Treats import charges on DL-4018 as Import billing's decision, to be made when the parcel reaches the depot, and not yet made

Carries the customs-slip fact to where it matters: either tells Import billing the original customs slip is reported to be on the returned box, or tells the shipper that Import billing has said it needs the customs paperwork from the original shipment
must_not: States that she is, or is not, legally obliged to refund the outbound postage, or cites a law, cooling-off period or marketplace rule as settling it
States that DL-4018 will, or will not, be charged import duty
Tells her the customs slip is irrelevant or can be thrown away
Tells her what to say to Stallfront or the buyer
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: Following your note of 4 March on DL-4018 (buyer's return of DL-8965, shipper Jory Lumley, due at the Destination depot around 6 March): the outbound reference is DL-8965, delivered in Veldmark on 9 February. The shipper has been told by the buyer that the original Veldmark customs slip from DL-8965 is still taped to the returning box. Is that the paperwork you need for the returned-goods assessment, and is there anything else she should have ready? She has a marketplace deadline of 10 March and needs to know whether a charge will be raised, so could you tell me when after arrival you expect to assess it? I have not told her whether charges will apply.
